subject: Acme POC Kickoff — Recap & Next Steps
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex_martinez@redwood.ai>
To: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@acme.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 21 Mar 2026 15:00:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Kickoff — Recap & Next Steps

Thanks again for the time today — great conversation. Below is a concise recap from our call and proposed next steps so we can get the PoC running next week. Please reply to confirm or flag anything missing.

Summary of pain points (what Acme told us):
- Production latency spikes on customer-facing chat during peak windows (90th pct latency ~ 1.2s, occasional >2s).
- Token cost is high for the throughput they need; team losing predictability in unit economics when scaling.
- Need stronger auditability / SSO & role-based access for model access in regulated regions.

PoC goals (success metrics):
1) Reduce 90th percentile latency by >= 30% for the customer chat route (baseline: 1.2s)
2) Achieve >= 25% reduction in per-token cost for the main inference workload (measured over 1 week of production-like traffic)
3) Validate end-to-end secure access with SSO + KMS integration and logging for audit (SLO: evidence of logs and keys bound to Acme account)

Scope of the PoC (what Redwood will deliver):
- Hosted Dedicated tenant with a reserved pool matching their expected concurrency for testing (config TBD).
- Model variants: run benchmarks on model-a / model-a-quant (our recommended profiles) and provide recommended quantization profile.
- Prompt set & evals: Redwood will run the attached prompt_set.csv and eval_suite.yml against the baseline model and the optimized serving config.
- Instrumentation: latency and token-cost dashboards in Redwood Console; access to trace links for 30 days.

Owners & contacts:
- Acme: John Smith (Product) — overall PM and acceptance sign-off; Priya Rao (SRE) — infra + SSO/KMS contact.
- Redwood: Alex Martinez (AM) — PoC day-to-day lead; Marissa Cole (Solutions Eng) — integration & evals; Aditya Rao (Security Eng) — SSO/KMS evidence.

Timeline (proposed):
- Tue 2026-03-23: Data + SSO access handed off by Acme (see Access steps)
- Wed 2026-03-24: Dedicated tenant provisioned and baseline benchmarking completed
- Thu-Fri 2026-03-25–26: Prompt/eval runs and tuning
- Mon 2026-03-29: Results review & acceptance criteria check; next steps (rollout or iterate)

Access / setup steps required from Acme:
1) Add alex_martinez@redwood.ai and marissa_cole@redwood.ai to Acme Okta as a SAML test application admin (temporary test accounts)
2) Share sample traffic logs & representative prompt set (S3 presigned link or Drive folder) — we only need anonymized examples for evals
3) Provide a service account with read-only access to the dataset location or an export of ~10k representative requests

Attachments: Acme_PoC_Plan_v1.docx (detailed scope), acme_prompt_set.csv, eval_suite.yml

Next steps (ask):
- John/Priya: please confirm SSO owner and whether you can share the sample data by Tue EOD.
- If confirmed, we’ll provision the tenant on Wed and send calendar invites for the kickoff checkpoints.

Thanks — looking forward to driving quick results.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex_martinez@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0198

From: John Smith <john.smith@acme.com>

Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC Kickoff — Recap & Next Steps

Alex — thanks for the clear recap. Confirming the PoC goals and timeline look good from our side. A few clarifications: 
- We can share anonymized logs by Tue EOD; SRE wants to confirm the exact IAM role needed (I’ll loop Priya).
- For SSO, our Okta admin (Priya) will add your test accounts. We prefer not to share production keys; we’ll create a test KMS key scoped to the PoC.
- Can you confirm which model variant is the baseline you’ll compare against? Need that for our internal procurement note.

Also, one ask: could you add an acceptance criterion that checks semantic coherency for customer-facing chat (simple quality threshold like average BLEU/EM or a qualitative sample review)? We don’t want latency at the cost of quality.

Thanks — John
